Alex (customer): hitting intermittent JSON parsing failures when using json_mode with streaming. Error surfaces as JSONDecodeError in our pydantic-based pipeline.

Alex (customer): repro (stream=true):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXXX\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\n    \"model\":\"rw-infer/chat-1.2\",\n    \"json_mode\": true,\n    \"schema\": {\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"id\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"score\":{\"type\":\"number\"}},\"required\":[\"id\",\"score\"]},\n    \"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"label this\"}],\n    \"stream\": true\n  }'
```

Alex (customer): app error: "JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 12 (char 11)"

Maya R: can you share the request-id and any raw streamed chunks?

support-bot: request 01H9A1B2 served by rw-node-7 in us-west-2, latency 168ms, tokens 142

Alex (customer): request-id 01H9A1B2. Attached raw stream tail: (pasted below)

Sara I: raw tail we pulled from node logs:
```
...{"id":"xyz001","score":0.81},
{"id":"xyz002","score":"0.92"},
{"id":"xyz003","score":0.76,}
```

Sara I: three problems visible: 1) score sometimes a string, 2) trailing comma after 0.76, 3) occasional control char sequences around chunk boundaries (e.g. "\x0b"). Those will break strict JSON parsers.

Priya S: causes could be model finishing tokens with punctuation near chunk boundaries or greedy sampling emitting extra separators. Also streaming framing can split tokens mid-escape sequence.

Jordan L: customer mentions they use Pydantic v1 with strict types; that will fail on the string-number mismatch. Also they reported duplicate processing and billing because their consumer retried on parse errors and our callbacks were delivered twice.

Alex (customer): correct — our handler retried, then downstream callbacks duplicated. Can Redwood provide a stable response identifier header so we can dedupe?

Maya R: immediate mitigation suggestions for customer: 1) switch to non-streaming for critical flows until we remediate; 2) implement tolerant client-side sanitization before JSON parse; 3) dedupe using response id when available. Example tolerant parser we shared:
```
import json, re
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError
raw = raw_streamed_string
# remove obvious trailing commas before closing brace/bracket
raw = re.sub(r",\s+([}\]])", r"\1", raw)
# drop C0 control chars that can break parsers
raw = re.sub(r"[\\x00-\\x1f]", "", raw)
obj = json.loads(raw)
Model.parse_obj(obj)
```

Priya S: platform-side actions: enable sanitizer on canary nodes for rw-infer/chat-1.2 to strip trailing commas and control chars at chunk assembly time, and emit a log warning when sanitization is applied. Also add an optional json_mode flag "strict": false|true so customers can opt into strict validation (server will reject responses that don't exactly match schema when strict=true).

Jordan L: agree. Also infra task: add model integration test that simulates split token boundaries producing malformed fragments and ensure sanitizer covers common cases. Assign to eng-ml + eng-runtime.

Sara I: about response id header: we'll add "x-rw-response-id" to both streaming events and final response metadata. Will run canary for 24h.

Maya R: follow-ups for support:
- Reply to customer with workaround + sample tolerant code and note that we will enable canary sanitizer + header within 48h.
- Escalate billing duplicate-charge report to finance; mark ticket for dedupe guidance.
- Track eng tasks: ENABLE_SANITIZER_CANARY, ADD_JSONMODE_STRICT_FLAG, ADD_RESPONSE_ID_HEADER, ADD_STREAM_PARSE_TESTS.

support-bot: ticket 99821 escalated to support-urgent, SLA updated to 6h.

Alex (customer): appreciate the quick triage. We'll implement client-side cleanup and hold off retries for now. Please post canary result.

Maya R: will follow up after canary. Closing interim loop. :thumbsup:
